chunks: And from him, from Muhammad ibn Sahl, from his father, from Ishaq ibn Abdillah, who said:

I asked Abu al-Hasan Musa (peace be upon him) about the Mutamatti' (one performing Hajj al-Tamattu') who enters Mecca on the Day of Tarwiyah, so he said: 'For the Mutamatti' is [the time] between it and the night.'

key_terms.أَبَا الْحَسَنِ مُوسَى: Abu al-Hasan Musa (Imam Musa al-Kazim, peace be upon him)
key_terms.الْمُتَمَتِّعِ: Mutamatti' (one who performs Hajj al-Tamattu', combining Umrah and Hajj)
key_terms.وَبَيْنَ اللَّيْلِ: And until the night (indicating the duration of the initial Ihram period)
key_terms.يَوْمَ التَّرْوِيَةِ: Day of Tarwiyah (8th of Dhu al-Hijjah)

ai.seo_question: When does the Ihram for Hajj al-Tamattu' begin if one enters Mecca on the Day of Tarwiyah?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam Musa al-Kazim clarifies the temporal boundary for the Ihram of Hajj al-Tamattu', specifying that upon entering Mecca on the 8th of Dhu al-Hijjah, the pilgrim remains in the state of Ihram until nightfall. This ruling underscores the distinct legal status of the Mutamatti' compared to the Qarin and Qadim, ensuring the continuity of their sacred state before the specific rites of the Day of Arafah commence. It highlights the precision with which the Imams delineated ritual timings to maintain the sanctity of the pilgrimage rites.
